correctness.rationale: A complete integer matrix proof, not extrapolation: the Perrin trace equals tr(M^n); \\(\\(M^7\\)\\)=I+2B and \\(M^{14}\\)=I+4C with odd trace certificates (5,17) and (7,29) for j=1,3. Odd and even index differences have valuations 1+\\(\\\\(\\\\(\\nu_2\\)\\)(u-v)\\) by exact modular division and repeated squaring. Each parity section has exactly \\(2^{k-1}\\) pairwise distinct values, hence covers its parity ball; determinant -23 of the three cyclic initial vectors yields least period. The included standalone checker passed 11,956 grouped finite tests, which are supporting checks rather than the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: No covering claim located for the two exact 2-adic Perrin residue sections or their universal pairwise valuation law. Period tables are insufficient; the 2024 shifted +1 valuation theorem concerns one target, and the published full-support Perrin result at prime three does not imply dyadic coverage. Herendi 2018 constructs uniformly distributed sequences under different characteristic-polynomial hypotheses, while Perrin parity counts are nonuniform. Historical priority remains qualified because one close 2024 source was available only in abstract and a general 2004 distribution paper only in bibliographic description.

Search failure is not a proof of priority; an equivalent earlier local-isometry formulation might exist under different terminology.

value.rationale: The precise dyadic value image and unique arithmetic-progression representatives are natural exact invariants of a classical linear recurrence. The full Perrin sequence has demonstrably unequal parity frequencies yet its two explicit subsequences partition the full 2-adic residue ring bijectively at every depth. The distance law gives a constructive stable inverse for every binary target, distinguishing the result from period tables, isolated congruences and known prime-three coverage; no broader application is claimed.
